{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./multi_acceljerk.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   -N 8                 -> -N 8
#   --ntasks-per-node 26  -> -n 208 (8*26)
#   -t 48:00:00          -> -t 48h
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 8 -n 208 -t 48h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm -p RM not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the RM partition.

  # NOTE: Slurm -A phy210030p not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: accounting/charging may not be applied as intended; site may require account/project out-of-band.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mail-type/--mail-user not translated.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: no email notifications.

  # NOTE: Slurm --output=...%j.log uses %j expansion (jobid) which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: logs may overwrite unless you generate unique filenames.

  module load openmpi/3.1.6-gcc8.3.1

  CMDDIR=$PROJECT/HPC_pulsar/cmd_files

  # Slurm used $SLURM_NTASKS; under Flux use the requested ranks.
  echo 208

  # Run within the allocation.
  flux run -n 208 "$CMDDIR/multinode_accelsearch.cmd"
fi
"
}
